front: Name the four short-axis parasternal levels from base to apex.
back: 1) Aortic valve. 2) Mitral valve. 3) Mid-papillary. 4) Apex.

front: Which parasternal short-axis level is the primary intraoperative view?
back: Mid-papillary level. Used for wall-motion assessment and volume status during surgery.

front: Which view is most sensitive for detecting an atrial septal defect on TTE?
back: Subcostal 4-chamber. The septum is imaged perpendicular to the beam, avoiding drop-out.

front: From which view do you assess the aortic arch and search for coarctation on TTE?
Name the six mitral leaflet segments.
back: Anterior: A1 (lateral), A2 (middle), A3 (medial). Posterior: P1 (lateral), P2 (middle), P3 (medial).

front: Name the three aortic valve cusps.
back: Right coronary cusp (RCC), Left coronary cusp (LCC), and Non-coronary cusp (NCC).

front: Which two LV walls are visualized in the apical 2-chamber view?
Which two LV walls are visualized in the apical 3-chamber (LAX) view?
back: Anteroseptal (or inferoseptal) and inferolateral (posterior). The LVOT is also seen.
